title: Electronic braking - Loss of braking torque
text: Item: Electronic braking. Malfunction: Loss of braking torque. Scenario: Highway approach to slow traffic. Hazard: Insufficient deceleration and rear-end collision. Safety goal: Prevent loss of commanded braking torque. FSR: The braking controller shall detect inconsistent brake actuator feedback and request the defined degraded mode within 100 ms. TSR: The feedback monitor shall compare commanded and measured torque every 10 ms and flag a mismatch lasting 50 ms. Verification: Inject missing actuator feedback and verify degraded-mode request within 100 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Electronic braking - Unintended braking
text: Item: Electronic braking. Malfunction: Unintended braking. Scenario: Dry highway with following traffic. Hazard: Unexpected deceleration and following-vehicle collision. Safety goal: Prevent unintended braking torque. FSR: The braking controller shall reject a brake torque command that fails plausibility checks within 100 ms. TSR: The command monitor shall check range and pedal correlation every 10 ms. Verification: Inject an out-of-range torque request and verify command rejection within 100 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Electric power steering - Loss of steering assistance
text: Item: Electric power steering. Malfunction: Loss of steering assistance. Scenario: Low speed parking manoeuvre. Hazard: Increased steering effort and contact with obstacle. Safety goal: Maintain controllable steering during assistance loss. FSR: The steering controller shall indicate assistance loss to the driver within 500 ms. TSR: The diagnostic monitor shall detect missing assist motor feedback within 100 ms. Verification: Disconnect motor feedback and verify driver indication within 500 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Electric power steering - Unintended steering torque
text: Item: Electric power steering. Malfunction: Unintended steering torque. Scenario: Highway lane keeping. Hazard: Lane departure and collision. Safety goal: Prevent unintended steering torque. FSR: The steering controller shall disable assistance on a confirmed torque plausibility fault within 50 ms. TSR: The torque monitor shall compare two independent sensor channels every 5 ms. Verification: Inject a torque sensor disagreement and verify assistance disable within 50 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Electronic throttle - Unintended acceleration
text: Item: Electronic throttle. Malfunction: Unintended acceleration. Scenario: Urban pedestrian crossing. Hazard: Vehicle acceleration into pedestrian path. Safety goal: Prevent acceleration without valid driver demand. FSR: The propulsion controller shall limit torque on an accelerator sensor disagreement within 100 ms. TSR: The pedal monitor shall compare redundant pedal channels every 10 ms. Verification: Inject pedal channel disagreement and verify torque limitation within 100 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Electronic throttle - Loss of propulsion
text: Item: Electronic throttle. Malfunction: Loss of propulsion. Scenario: Highway overtaking. Hazard: Loss of acceleration while exposed to traffic. Safety goal: Preserve a controlled transition on propulsion loss. FSR: The propulsion controller shall provide a loss-of-propulsion warning within 300 ms. TSR: The drive monitor shall detect commanded torque without measured drive response within 100 ms. Verification: Suppress drive response during a simulated overtake and verify warning within 300 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Exterior lighting - Loss of headlamps
text: Item: Exterior lighting. Malfunction: Loss of headlamps. Scenario: Night road without street lighting. Hazard: Reduced road visibility and obstacle collision. Safety goal: Maintain adequate forward illumination. FSR: The lighting controller shall command available redundant illumination and issue a warning within 200 ms after a lamp fault. TSR: The lamp monitor shall check current feedback every 20 ms. Verification: Disconnect a headlamp in the night scenario and verify fallback command within 200 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Exterior lighting - Brake lamps remain off
text: Item: Exterior lighting. Malfunction: Brake lamps remain off. Scenario: Urban traffic during deceleration. Hazard: Following driver misses braking cue. Safety goal: Indicate braking to following traffic. FSR: The lighting controller shall activate the available brake lamp channel within 100 ms of a valid braking request. TSR: The brake lamp monitor shall diagnose an open circuit within 50 ms. Verification: Inject an open brake lamp circuit and verify alternate-channel activation within 100 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Battery management - Invalid charge current command
text: Item: Battery management. Malfunction: Invalid charge current command. Scenario: Stationary charging. Hazard: Overcurrent due to erroneous electronic control. Safety goal: Prevent excessive charging current caused by a control fault. FSR: The battery controller shall request charge isolation within 100 ms of a confirmed overcurrent control fault. TSR: The current monitor shall compare sensor readings with the configured synthetic current limit every 10 ms. Verification: Inject an invalid charging command and verify isolation request within 100 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Battery management - Unexpected contactor opening
text: Item: Battery management. Malfunction: Unexpected contactor opening. Scenario: Highway cruise. Hazard: Sudden propulsion interruption and collision risk. Safety goal: Prevent unintended high-voltage disconnection. FSR: The battery controller shall reject a contactor-open command without a valid fault or shutdown condition. TSR: The contactor monitor shall verify command authorization and state feedback every 10 ms. Verification: Inject an unauthorized open command and verify it is rejected. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Instrument cluster - Missing speed indication
text: Item: Instrument cluster. Malfunction: Missing speed indication. Scenario: Urban driving near speed restriction. Hazard: Driver lacks speed feedback and overspeeds. Safety goal: Provide a visible indication of speed signal loss. FSR: The cluster shall display a speed signal fault within 1000 ms of invalid speed data. TSR: The communication monitor shall mark a speed signal invalid after 200 ms without a valid update. Verification: Drop speed messages and verify fault display within 1000 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Reverse assistance - False distance information
text: Item: Reverse assistance. Malfunction: False distance information. Scenario: Low speed reversing near a pedestrian. Hazard: Collision with a pedestrian behind the vehicle. Safety goal: Avoid misleading reverse distance information. FSR: The reverse assistant shall suppress invalid distance values and indicate unavailable assistance within 200 ms. TSR: The sensor monitor shall reject distance values that fail configured plausibility checks. Verification: Inject a false-clear distance value and verify unavailable-assistance indication within 200 ms. All thresholds and ratings are synthetic examples, not validated vehicle limits.

title: Item definition
text: An item definition records the system boundary, functions, interfaces, dependencies, intended operating conditions and assumptions. The synthetic electronic braking item accepts pedal requests, controls brake torque and monitors actuator feedback. The prototype does not read a real ECU.

title: Hazard and hazardous event
text: A hazard describes potential harm caused by malfunctioning behaviour. A hazardous event combines the hazard with an operational situation. Loss of braking during a highway approach is different from the same malfunction while parked. Operational context must accompany each assessment.

title: Severity exposure and controllability
text: Severity S describes the potential consequence. Exposure E concerns the occurrence of the operational situation, not the probability of the component failure. Controllability C concerns the ability of people involved to avoid harm. Ratings require evidence and expert judgment. This demo accepts integer S 0 to 3, E 0 to 4 and C 0 to 3.

title: Synthetic risk rules
text: The candidate ASIL lookup is an authored educational table for the demo. It returns QM for S0, E0 or C0, and otherwise uses the configured table. QM denotes the demo quality-management category. The table is not an approved interpretation of ISO 26262. No automatic safety classification is authorized. The rule version and user rationale are retained.

title: Safety goals and requirements
text: A safety goal states the high-level intent to avoid a hazardous event. Functional safety requirements define the required behaviour; technical safety requirements allocate implementation behaviour. Each draft must state a subject, shall, a condition and a verifiable action. Timing and test criteria must be justified before engineering use.

title: Traceability
text: Mandatory demo links run from hazardous event to safety goal, then FSR, TSR and verification test. A complete chain means every referenced node exists; it does not establish technical correctness. A missing test is a traceability gap. When a requirement changes, review all downstream tests and invalidate its prior student review.

title: Human review and audit
text: Every generated artifact starts in PENDING_REVIEW. A student may record STUDENT_REVIEWED or REJECTED with a reviewer name and reason. STUDENT_REVIEWED is not faculty approval, safety approval or release authorization. The local SQLite audit log records creation, review and update events; it is not tamper-proof.

title: Grounded responses and limits
text: Evidence mode returns source text from the local knowledge base with bracketed citations. Local LLM mode uses retrieved text and returns a draft; matching citation IDs alone does not prove claim-level faithfulness. The system refuses queries with no adequate lexical evidence. Synthetic examples cannot establish ISO compliance or certify a vehicle.

title: Data provenance and privacy
text: The corpus contains authored synthetic automotive scenarios and original teaching notes. It contains no personal information, licensed standard text or confidential production vehicle data. The provided internal-use case-study PDF is a planning reference and is not embedded or redistributed with the public code.

title: Change impact and quality
text: A change to a safety requirement requires review of its dependent technical requirement and verification test. The quality checker flags missing shall, vague wording such as fast or appropriate, and missing measurable criteria. These are text heuristics and cannot verify completeness of a safety concept.
